text: Four people, one small board. What brought them together? This is yutnori, a Korean game played with four wooden sticks instead of dice. Players move their pieces around a board, choosing routes and trying to send every piece home. A lucky throw helps, but a smart choice matters too. Traditionally played around the Lunar New Year, the game brings families and neighbors together. Nineteenth-century visitors to Korea collected pictures of everyday life: work, clothing, and moments like this. Such a scene could introduce an unfamiliar country through something familiar: playing together. This work is attributed to Uncho. Watch the hands and the circle of players. From the TJ Kim Collection, a small game opens a window onto Korean life.
